answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line runs at 94% with zero buffer, so downstream assembly is already exposed. Switching primary or standing up a second source would change the physical supply path under that constraint and would increase delivery risk; last year's low-cost cut and quick onboarding do not establish that a cutover is safe in two weeks. Deferral is a mismatch: this renewal is volume-critical, unlike the non-critical month-to-month case. Incumbent continuity previously avoided migration and missed deliveries. The one action that can pursue the 18% TCO mandate without changing who ships parts is a benchmarked renegotiation at renewal, optionally using term/volume for price, while keeping the incumbent on the line. Whether 18% is actually achievable is unknown; that uncertainty is preserved pending archive checks of c4 and c1.
